title: India's Financial Shield: What Are Our Foreign Exchange Reserves?

faq.q: How much are India's foreign exchange reserves right now?
faq.a: As of the week ending June 5, 2026, India's foreign exchange reserves stood at $681.610 billion.

faq.q: What are the main parts of these reserves?
faq.a: The main components are Foreign Currency Assets (like US Dollars, Euros), Gold Reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and India's Reserve Tranche Position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

faq.q: Who manages India's foreign exchange reserves?
faq.a: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for managing and maintaining India's foreign exchange reserves.

faq.q: Why did India's forex reserves decrease recently?
faq.a: For the week ending June 5, 2026, the decrease was primarily due to a decline in Foreign Currency Assets, even though gold reserves saw an increase. Changes can be due to RBI intervention, valuation changes of non-US currencies, or capital flows.

faq.q: Do other countries also hold foreign exchange reserves?
faq.a: Yes, most countries hold foreign exchange reserves. They are a standard tool for central banks to manage their economies and maintain financial stability.
